fields.Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "Music as a devolved system, not an evolved one", "body": "Jorge Mesa returns to InnerVerse after 25 years of teaching Western music theory to argue that music has not evolved so much as it has been devolved on purpose. He tells Chance Garton that everything he learned in music college was essentially German and Austrian church music, a rule set handed down rather than discovered. The 432 versus 440 hertz debate is his opening example, but he refuses to treat 432 as a cure. If that number alone saved people, he says, humanity would have been saved already. The deeper problem is that fixing any note as the letter A is itself a construct."}, {"title": "Limitless pitch narrowed to twelve frets", "body": "Jorge compares the note wheel to a color wheel. Everyone accepts that there are limitless colors between colors, yet pianos and fretted instruments quietly train us to accept only twelve pitches out of an infinite field. He explains equal temperament, where the octave is split into twelve equal steps so every note can serve as a tonal center, and notes that this convenience destroys the true proportions the overtone series calls for. Tuning a guitar to 432 and then playing rock music, he tells Chance, changes very little. The real practice is finding a fundamental pitch and resonating with everything inside it."}, {"title": "Tonal centers, ragas and the loss of free meter", "body": "Before Western notation, Jorge says, melody had a tonal center you danced around and came home to, the way a sitar's sympathetic strings or a bagpipe drone hold one pitch. Rhythm was not locked to meter. A raga and a tala left interpretation to the singer, so the same song carried human inflection every time instead of metronome precision. Chance Garton takes the word meter apart, linking it to Metis and to wisdom, and suggests a bar of music is a gate you pass through. Jorge adds that the Torah and Koran were meant to be chanted, every syllable a musical phrase."}, {"title": "Inversion, triads and the missing third", "body": "The episode's sharpest claim is inversion. Jorge says minor was once heard as joyful and major as serious, pointing to Hava Nagila as a minor melody meaning let us rejoice, and argues we were retrained to hear major as happy and minor as sad. He demonstrates on bass that two notes sound major until a third note flips them to minor, and Chance reads that third note as Mercury, the sun, the deciding polarity. Power chords strip the third out entirely, which Chance calls body and mind with no spirit, a transhuman music with no dissonance and no tension to resolve."}, {"title": "The zodiac wheel drawn as a chord chart", "body": "Jorge's original work maps the twelve signs onto the twelve pitches, rotating the wheel so C sits at the top because C is the Bible key of Western music and Aries is the fourth sign from Capricorn. Trines of the same element then spell augmented triads, and squares spell diminished triads, exactly the two chord types Western music uses least. He also finds that stacking pure fifths overshoots the circle and lands on 365.04 rather than 360. Chance closes with Dylan Saccoccio and the numerology of 432, 108 and the Fibonacci cycle, plus Paganini, Liszt and Masonic composers along the way."}]
fields.Intro Paragraph 1: Jorge Mesa of Third Eye Edify returns to talk about Western Musical Theory: the good, the bad, and the muddy. We discuss 432hz, the musical zodiac, audio alchemy, octaves, scales, triads, chords, and the mythos of the origins of music theory. And there is way more than that, in this extra-long episode! Best of all, Jorge plays the bass in this one!
fields.Intro Paragraph 2: In the oversized Plus+ Extension, some topics include the pitch, the overtone series and fractals! We riff on modern music and the cultures around genres, frequency warfare, solfeggio, the language of notation, teaching, and musical archetypes.
